text:
(There is an addendum below regarding a Line reply from the clinic after this review. Please judge for yourselves which provides a more "specific" explanation. Also, this kind of paranoid overreaction to specific negative reviews is the easiest way to spot a fool, so please use it as a reference.) (The clinic owner also added stealthily false explanations, so I've added a point about that at the end.)

I had my family's teeth examined, and they performed an X-ray, diagnosis, and treatment proposal. Their titles and achievements on the website are impressive, but unfortunately, I absolutely cannot recommend them. Unless you are wealthy and easily deceived, their sincerity is clearly lacking, so I want to reiterate this warning. I'm pointing out that their subsequent handling of the situation was even worse based on my personal experience.

The reason is that all solutions were based on the premise of implants. Even though the survival rate for teeth with poor prognosis is 80-95% at 10 years, and implants are 90-95%, they proposed extracting all 11 of my upper teeth, including teeth with good prognosis, and then suggesting implants.

Furthermore, when I inquired about this via Line, I received prompt replies up until then. However, when I asked about the basis for the above diagnosis and treatment plan, along with the evidence, the communication stopped, and even reminders were ignored. I was probably ignored as a patient who wouldn't fall for the trick.

Ultimately, at another clinic where I sought a second opinion, they proposed extracting two teeth and using a bridge with zirconia crowns for the rest. I was understandably quite angry at the dentist who had proposed extracting all 11 teeth and using All-on-4 implants. A third opinion was obtained, and it was the same as the second. In the end, I completed treatment at the second clinic in three weeks.

This is a perfect example of Maslow's hammer/tool ​​law ("To someone with only a hammer, everything looks like a nail").

Whether this clinic or dentist had malicious intent or not, from the patient's perspective, it's unethical. It only results in loss.

Everyone, be careful of places with only positive reviews and a good track record. Good reviews can be fabricated, so judge the quality based on the likelihood of negative reviews.


(Postscript) After posting this review, I received a reply via Line.

It was abusive, without answering any specific questions, just insults like, "You can keep searching until you find the diagnosis and treatment you want," and a baseless excuse that "what's important is being satisfied with your condition 5 or 10 years from now."

Furthermore, despite asking in the email about the meaning of extracting 11 teeth, including perfectly healthy ones, they dismissed it as merely online statistics as evidence. They also failed to answer my second question, asking how implants could outweigh the treatment plan of extracting two teeth and using a bridge, considering the condition of my teeth and gums. It was just a harassing Line message, abstractly asserting their own righteousness.

A person's true character is determined not by how they behave when things are going well, but by how they act when problems arise.

Confirming this clinic's insidious and utterly dishonest attitude, I am truly relieved that I sought a second and third opinion.

Everyone, beware of this turret. Even those who underwent implant treatment without listening to explanations other than those related to implants may, if a problem arises, completely ignore the other party's claims and refuse to answer questions (which is understandable since they can't answer because there's no valid reason). Remember, the medical service industry has high negative switching costs. Choose carefully.

For reference, since the owner (clinic director) shared this in a comment, I will also share my reply to the owner here.



You say I kept asking irrelevant questions, but I only asked two questions.

Furthermore, my second question was simply to clarify a point that was ignored in the first answer. I received no response, and the fact remains that I was simply ignored.

You also claim that the guidelines, which form an important part of the treatment plan, are merely statistical data from the internet. However, the problem is that you are ignoring the evidence in the first place.

Furthermore, while you claim that appropriate treatment depends on the patient's condition, the information provided here is extremely superficial. The other two clinics also estimate that the number of teeth requiring extraction will be at most around two.

Conversely, if you have any specific professional opinions that contradict this—opinions that justify extracting the remaining nine teeth, which are not the ones that need extraction, in order to proceed with implants—please point them out. I would appreciate extremely specific explanations, not vague or abstract opinions. Since you did not answer my second question, which was intended to clarify something unclear in your first reply, I understand that such an opinion does not exist.

Conversely, if you have any specific professional opinions that justify extracting the remaining nine teeth, which are not the ones that need extraction, in order to proceed with implants, please point them out. I would appreciate extremely specific explanations, not vague or abstract opinions.

I understand that such an opinion does not exist, given that you did not answer my second question from last time.



<>
1. Prognosis for individual teeth
Could you please provide the following clinical data for the eight maxillary teeth (#11, 12, 14, 16, 21, 22, 23, 25)?
• Periodontal pocket depth (PPD) and clinical attachment level (CAL)
• Bone resorption rate
• Mobility (Miller classification)
• Remaining tooth structure and ferrule height
• Prognosis category based on the McGuire & Nunn (1996) or Kwok & Caton (2007) classification (good/average/poor/doubtful/hopeless)

2. Urgency of tooth #21
Please provide specific clinical evidence (including remaining dentin thickness (mm), ferrule height, and occlusal contact with opposing teeth) that supports the view that tooth #21 "may fall out in a few days or months."

3. Tooth Preservation Options
Could you please explain specifically why each of the following options is not applicable to each tooth?
• Crown lengthening or biological shaping
• Deep margin elevation (DME)
• Periodontal tissue regeneration therapy (EMD/GTR) — In a 10-year RCT by Cortellini et al. (J Clin Periodontol, 2020), the survival rate of teeth with a poor prognosis was 88%.
• Silver diamine fluoride (SDF) as a temporary measure to suppress caries progression
• Root canal treatment + post & core + crown for each tooth as a stepwise conservative treatment

4. Stepwise Treatment Options
Are the following stepwise approaches possible instead of full-mouth extraction?

• First, extract only the tooth with the worst prognosis.
• Maintain the remaining teeth with aggressive periodontal treatment and temporary crowns.
• Re-evaluate the possibility of restoration after 12 months.



None of these were answered, and instead, the owner gave abstract comments like those shown below. Especially point 1 is a fundamental concept; the inability to answer it means that treatment is being proposed without a proper diagnosis.

Were these questions repeated endlessly without any real meaning? (Furthermore, this question was only asked once, and there was no reply. I asked this question because the first reply lacked any specifics.)

(✳︎It seems the owner secretly edited the comment, so I will also point out the inaccuracies.

They added a lie, stating, "Our dentists carefully explained the rationale behind the proposed treatment, presented multiple options, and explained the risks and benefits of each treatment method." This is precisely why I asked the second question. In fact, I have received absolutely no answer to the main question I shared in the previous comment.

I am pointing this out because it is clearly a lie. They did not explain the individual tooth condition or alternative treatment options at all. They simply said, "All-on-4 is good, so get implants," and provided an estimate. They only offered implants. If you have a detailed explanation and alternative suggestions, please reply via Line.

The second and third opinion clinics are not affiliated with this clinic, but it's understandable that they were upset and angry about the proposals this clinic made.

Again, there are many clinics in Pattaya with Google reviews of 4.8 or 4.9. What's important is the situation with the low reviews and the clinic's specific explanations and responses to them.

Honestly, I understand your desire to continue defending your position despite these facts, but you should reflect on and acknowledge that speaking ill of potential patients for vague and abstract reasons is damaging the clinic's reputation.

That's all.
